definition: The shared tokens, components, patterns, documentation and the people and processes that keep them current, so many teams can build consistent interfaces without re-deciding everything.
An audit that collects every instance of each UI element across products, grouped by type, to make duplication visible and to decide what a design system should own first.
A short statement that picks a side in a real trade-off, such as accessible before beautiful, so it can settle design arguments without a long meeting.
A way of running a design system in which a small dedicated core owns tokens, reviews and releases while product teams contribute components and fixes through a defined process.
A named design decision, such as a color, spacing value or font size, stored once and referenced by name from design tools and code instead of repeating raw values.
A token that names a raw value by what it is, such as `--nw-blue-600`, without saying where it is used. Primitives form the system's palette and scales.
A token that names an intent, such as `--nw-color-action-bg`, and points at a primitive. Themes and brands change which primitive each semantic token points at.
A token scoped to one component, such as `--nw-button-bg`, that points at a semantic token and lets that component be adjusted without affecting others.
A fixed order of name parts, such as category, concept, property, variant and state, that makes token names predictable to guess, sortable, and checkable by a lint rule.
A remapping of semantic tokens to different primitives, such as a dark theme, applied with a selector like `[data-theme="dark"]` while components stay unchanged.
An independent dimension of theming, such as color scheme, brand or density, that owns its own set of tokens so combinations compose without separate files for each.
The JSON format for design tokens defined by the W3C Design Tokens Community Group, whose first stable version, 2025.10, covers tokens, types, groups, aliases and color.
A token whose value refers to another token by its path in curly braces, such as `{color.blue.600}`. It must point at a token, never at a group.
A build step that parses token files, resolves aliases, transforms names and values per platform, and writes formats such as CSS custom properties, Swift and Kotlin.
A pipeline setting that keeps aliases as `var()` references in generated CSS instead of resolved values, so the token tiers and runtime overrides survive into the browser.
One of a fixed set of mutually exclusive styles of a component, such as primary, secondary or danger, best expressed as a single enum prop rather than separate booleans.
A place in a component where the consumer passes content, such as `children` or a `startIcon` element, instead of configuring that content through more props.
A component made of cooperating pieces, such as `Tabs.List` and `Tabs.Trigger`, that the consumer arranges freely while the pieces share state through context.
A grid of every variant against every interaction state, such as hover, focus visible, disabled, loading and pressed, used to design, build and test a component completely.
A CSS pseudo-class that matches when the browser decides focus should be visible, typically after keyboard navigation, used to show focus rings without showing them on most mouse clicks.
One of several sets of values for the variables in a Figma collection, such as Light and Dark, applied to frames the way theme selectors apply to page sections.
A MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH version scheme where patches fix bugs, minors add backward-compatible features, and majors contain changes that can break existing usage.
A small file added to a pull request that states the version bump a change needs and a consumer-facing summary, later combined into the release version and changelog.
Marking an API, token or component as scheduled for removal while it still works, naming its replacement and removal version so teams can migrate before it disappears.
A script that rewrites source code automatically, such as renaming a deprecated prop across a repository, so migrations become reviews instead of manual work.
A test that screenshots a component state and compares it with an approved baseline, failing on differences that a human then accepts as intended or rejects as bugs.
A written proposal for a significant change, such as a new component, laying out the problem, evidence, API sketch and accessibility plan for open review before building.
A small layer of tokens between primitives and semantic tokens, such as a color ramp, fonts and radii, that each brand points at its own values.
The share of UI elements in a product that are rendered by the real design system components, measured with signals only those components produce, tracked as a trend.
